item.title: No One Was “Picasso’s Woman”
item.description: South Africa axes a performance about the genocide in Gaza, the real lives of the women who loved Picasso, the imaginative worlds of Rousseau, and Beer With a Painter.

item.title: Visions of Venezuela and Cuba From Exile
item.description: An exhibition near Washington, DC, offers an immersive reclamation of memory and identity in all their fluidity and impermanence.

item.title: Apply for IDSVA’s Low-Residency PhD in Visual Arts: Philosophy, Aesthetics, and Art Theory
item.description: The Institute for Doctoral Studies in the Visual Arts is accepting applications for September 2026.

item.title: The Contemporary Relevance of Palestinian Tatreez
item.description: “When people wear Palestinian embroidery, it’s not just decorative. It's beautiful, of course, but it is saying something,” says author Joanna Barakat.

item.title: Mitchell Johnson: Two San Francisco Exhibitions of Large-Scale Paintings
item.description: The Bay Area artist opens 2026 with “Large New England Landscapes (Selected Paintings 2008-2025)” and “Giant Abstract and Landscape Works (Selected Paintings 2012-2025).”

item.title: David Wojnarowicz in the Age of Surveillance
item.description: Books on the living tradition of Palestinian embroidery, the women artists whose legacies Picasso eclipsed, and more to kick off 2026.

item.title: The Nightmares Beneath the Surface of "Dreamworlds"
item.description: The traumas of war and genocide and the fascist leanings of Salvador Dalí are among the subjects that this sprawling exhibition leaves out.

item.title: A Video Game Lets You Take Back Looted Artifacts
item.description: An indie game studio in South Africa has developed a heist adventure that reframes play, memory, and repatriation.

item.title: Ms. Rachel Sells Artworks by Children From Gaza
item.description: The works are part of a new benefit exhibition organized by the global early childhood education star, a vocal supporter of Palestinian children.

item.title: Beatriz González, Colombian Painter of Collective Memory, Dies at 93
item.description: While often associated with Pop Art, her practice was rooted in the specificities of local visual culture, depicting political events, violence, and loss.
